Frontend: FleetDrivers page + Invite modal + Copy-link + FleetOverview live-map all verified visually (mobile 390x844, live URL). E2E trip lifecycle validated end-to-end at API layer (passenger POST /trips/request → driver GET /driver/pending sees it → POST /driver/accept transitions to driver_on_way with driver.plate=EL12345 & driver.car='Tesla Model Y' → driver GPS heartbeat propagates driver_lat/lng to trip → /driver/trip/{id}/start → in_trip → /arrive → arrived with correct price). Fleet driver-invite: POST /api/fleet/driver-invites returns token+fleet_id, GET /fleet/driver-invites lists scoped invites, 403 for regular user. GET /api/fleet/drivers now returns fullName, plate, car, online, last_lat, last_lng, last_heading, today_income, today_trips as required by UI. FleetOverview /fleet: PremiumMap renders as fleet-live-map (390x260), overlay chip correctly displays '1 sjåfør på vakt' when sjafor is online with GPS ping. FleetDrivers /fleet/drivers: all 4 testids (tab-drivers, tab-invites, fleet-invite-open, fleet-drivers-back) present. After submit → modal closes, tab auto-switches to 'Invitasjoner · N' (mint highlight), new invite-row-{token.substr(0,8)} appears with correct email+car+plate+VENTER status pill, invite-copy-{token.substr(0,8)} button writes /driver-signup/{token} to clipboard and swaps to 'Kopiert!' feedback state.

integration_issues.flow: Invite modal submit on mobile viewport
integration_issues.issue: Cookie consent bar (fixed bottom, z-[10000]) overlaps the invite-submit button in the bottom-anchored modal sheet on 390x844, blocking pointer events until consent is dismissed. Real end-users on first visit cannot submit an invite without first dismissing consent. Consider raising modal z-index above cookie consent, or moving cookie consent to a higher stacking context that yields when a modal is open.

action_items: Cookie-consent overlay z-index issue blocks bottom-anchored modal submits on mobile — raise modal z above 10000 or auto-hide consent when a modal opens.

Review testid contract: review_request specified invite-row-{token} and invite-copy-{token}, but implementation slices to token.substr(0,8). Not blocking (tests updated to prefix-match) but the shorter suffix increases collision risk (2^48 space still very safe though). Consider aligning names or documenting the truncation.
critical_code_review_comments: FleetOverview.jsx polls /api/fleet/drivers every 10s but never guards against concurrent runs — if a request slows, a second interval may fire before first resolves. Consider ref-based in-flight flag or replace setInterval with recursive setTimeout after resolve.

FleetDrivers.jsx uses navigator.clipboard?.writeText without fallback — some in-app WebViews (WKWebView older iOS) do not expose clipboard API. Add document.execCommand('copy') fallback via a hidden <textarea> for wider mobile compatibility.
InviteModal has no email format validation — an invalid email just gets stored as-is and email_sent stays false. Add regex or Pydantic EmailStr on backend field to prevent junk.

Modal onClick={onClose} uses outer div + stopPropagation on inner — this bottom-sheet interaction should also close on hardware back button (Android) via history state; currently users on Android will pop the app instead of the sheet.

server.py:1130-1177 (/driver/accept) uses hashlib.md5 to generate a random-ish start position when driver has no GPS — this is deterministic per (trip_id, driver_id) which is fine, but the fake offset 0.006–0.018 degrees ≈ 0.7–2km would show a phantom car far from reality if the driver hasn't sent any GPS. In practice drivers must go online (which triggers GPS) before accepting, but hardening: reject accept if last_location_at is stale (>60s).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter 15 is stable. Key notes: (1) On mobile viewport, cookie-consent banner (z-[10000]) intercepts pointer events at the bottom — Playwright tests MUST pre-set localStorage.kjapp_cookie_consent='all' and reload before interacting with any bottom-anchored modal or footer button. (2) PremiumMap in FleetOverview renders 390x260 with correct chip overlay — WebGL tiles may not visually render in headless (black canvas is environmental, not a bug) but the count chip correctly reflects live driver state. (3) FleetDrivers invite-row-{X} and invite-copy-{X} testids use token.substr(0,8), NOT the full token — write prefix-match selectors. (4) /api/driver/accept requires the driver to have last_lat/last_lng set (otherwise falls back to md5-derived offset from pickup) — always POST /api/driver/location before /api/driver/accept in E2E scripts. (5) Driver 'online' state persists across test runs — remember to POST /api/driver/online {online: false} in teardown if a test relies on 'no driver online'. (6) Backend server.py file at 2609 lines — still monolithic; refactor overdue.
rca of the issue: N/A — all requested iter15 features implemented correctly. Only minor UX note: cookie-consent overlay can block modal submits on first-time mobile visitors (see integration_issues).
